direction.statement: Seek a contradiction at any hypothetical right-half zeta zero by proving an independent estimate incompatible with the original Riesz carrier’s forced source limit. Preserve Möbius signs, logarithmic phases and full frequency correlations through conditioned-energy estimates. Stronger zero-free regions narrow the remaining strip; the arithmetic saving is still open.

scopes.boundScope: Furthest checked carrier bound: at a=0,b=1, use the proved critical homogeneous exponent 2k(u+1)-k(k+1)/2+eps for every eps>0, with k>=2,u>=k. The complete initial allowance is at most B*p^beta, -1/2<=beta<0, with every homogeneous and descendant-energy premise discharged. Prime, padded-quotient and p^S<=X conditions are explicit. Constants and thresholds are unevaluated. Full signed correlations, sampling and block normalization remain; their combined saving is unproved. RH remains open.
scopes.sourceScope: Under the displayed hypothetical right-half-zero assumptions, the normalized original carrier has the prescribed negative-multiplicity source limit. This conditional source identity supplies one side of the proposed contradiction; its independent arithmetic counterpart remains open.
scopes.initialConditioningScope: The unweighted critical moment exponent plus every eps>0 holds for k>=2,u>=k at sufficiently large endpoints. For each k>=12 the full eligible degree window gives the actual imaginary-power product sum a saving 1/(128*k^2) throughout M^(2k-2)<=t<=M^(2k), M^4<=z<=4*M^4. Original Dirichlet blocks of length M^4 starting at M^4<=z<=2*M^4 have bound C*M^(4-1/(128*k^2)); every partial block has its explicit endpoint allowance. Both moments, all Gaussian tails, smoothing, Taylor errors and averaging masses are paid. Constants and thresholds are unevaluated for each fixed degree. Uniform degree costs, all-scale zeta growth and the combined Riesz weighted saving remain open. Finite Abel transport also preserves every nonnegative decreasing weight family, including literal zeta coefficients at nonnegative real part. The main term pays actual total weight and the endpoint only its initial weight. All Gaussian constants cost at most two after the actual moment root, uniformly for k>=12; moment constants and thresholds remain unevaluated. Finite descent now proves actual critical+defect moments at every X>=1 with cost A^n*k!, starting from the proved elementary factorial bound. One exponent decrement and one multiplier are chosen before the source exponent and constant. The profile multiplier is at most (2ku)^(7k) independently of iteration count; original C stays linear and outside the prime threshold. The sharper actual deep remainder also retains -defect*u/(u+1)*(b-a+H), upstream of the present half-depth relaxation. The global multiplier, decrement and cutoff depth still need degree bounds; uniform zeta growth and the zero-free union are unchanged.
scopes.exponentAuditScope: Exact normalization audit: after restoring the source scale, lowering the exponent changes only the deep remainder by the coarse-quotient power. Every original intermediate conditioned energy is identical. The complete scaled allowance is no larger when a full coarse window fits. This comparison bounds no intermediate energy and does not prove RH.
scopes.fullRecurrenceScope: The general original-carrier recurrence applies to every displayed finite scale pair a<=b and depth H. Both actual quotient moments use the proved first improved exponent; all intermediate energies remain in the full allowance. The default view uses the critical exponent plus positive epsilon and a proved negative initial profile under its deeper cutoff conditions. No net signed correlation saving or RH contradiction is asserted.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.n.summary: The actual coefficient, common physical length and every fixed filter are retained. The normalized error is at most u^(N+1) times two geometric rates with convergent divisor-mass constants, uniformly in the ordinate.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.t.label: The actual outer residual pieces vanish independently
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.t.summary: For every fixed polynomial filter and every 0<u<1, both newly discarded pieces of the actual residual have vanishing normalized response. No hypothetical zero or prime-cancellation premise is used.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.t.label: The whole narrowed cosine carrier retains negative multiplicity
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.t.summary: At exposed right-half zeros the constant-filter residual in the smaller window still tends to the full negative analytic multiplicity. No source margin is spent by deleting the outer pieces.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.r.label: The narrowed sum retains the exact coefficient and cosine phase
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.r.summary: The complete real response remains one actual signed coefficient times a nonnegative factorial envelope times the cosine of the full logarithmic product phase, summed over the exact narrowed support.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.r.label: Conditional RH closure from the whole narrowed floor
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszNarrowCarrier.r.summary: A cofinal real floor at least -c with c<1 for each whole narrowed exposed carrier implies Mathlib RH. This independent arithmetic bound remains an explicit open premise; source transport and exposed-zero selection are proved.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremePrimeCou.label: Physical-cutoff primes consume the exact logarithmic budget
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremePrimeCou.summary: For every squarefree label, its number of distinct primes at or above the physical cutoff times the actual length is at most log(n).

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremePrimeCou.label: Every fixed source scale has finitely many surviving extreme degrees
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremePrimeCou.summary: For each fixed 0<u<1, some fixed degree cap eventually bounds all nonzero labels in the actual narrowed band. The cap and threshold depend on u.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremeDegreeBo.label: Sufficiently many extreme primes give independent unnormalized decay
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszExtremeDegreeBo.summary: For every fixed 0<u<1, some degree K(u) makes every changing finite selection with at least K(u) physical-cutoff prime factors decay, with the original coefficient and every fixed filter. No zero premise is used.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.label: The four-prime geometric rate is strictly below one
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.summary: The exact rate 4*exp(-23/16) is positive and below one. It is an arithmetic component rate, not a numerical zero bound.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.label: The entire four-or-more-extreme-prime class is bounded
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.summary: For 0<u<exp(-1/2), the actual source-normalized response is bounded by (4*exp(-23/16))^N times u*A(P,1/4,65/64), uniformly in the ordinate and finite selection. All fixed factorial shifts and the physical floor remain.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.label: The actual normalized four-prime class vanishes independently
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeBoun.summary: Every changing finite selection with at least four prime factors at or above the physical cutoff has vanishing normalized response on 0<u<exp(-1/2), without a zero premise.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.label: Delete the paid class from the whole actual carrier
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.summary: The normalized difference between the narrowed carrier and the new residual tends to zero. The support is unchanged outside the proved interval, retaining all earlier cuts and their ranges.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.label: At most three physical-cutoff primes remain on the deletion interval
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.summary: For u<exp(-1/2), every surviving label has at most three prime factors at or above X_N. This does not bound the number of intermediate primes N^2<p<X_N.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.label: The reduced whole carrier retains the negative multiplicity source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.summary: At every exposed right-half zero, the constant-filter carrier after the adaptive deletion still tends to minus the full analytic multiplicity. The exact coefficient, phase and all-scale fallback remain.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.label: The reduced real carrier keeps its exact signed cosine sum
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.summary: The original signed Riesz coefficient multiplies the nonnegative factorial envelope and cos(gamma*log(n)) over the new actual support. This identity supplies no independent lower floor.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.label: Conditional RH closure from the whole remaining floor
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszFourExtremeDele.summary: A cofinal floor at least -c with c<1 for each whole exposed residual implies Mathlib RH. That independent arithmetic floor remains an explicit open premise.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.label: A general actual degree bound retains the complete source factor
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.summary: An arbitrary admissible tilt gives a norm allowance for the actual finite class with at least k physical-cutoff primes. Its explicit degree rate must be below one to give decay.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.label: The two-prime rate has an exact closed expression
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.summary: The rate is (8/3)*exp(-95/96); its separate checked comparison is strictly below one. This is an arithmetic decay rate, not a numerical zero bound.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.label: The actual two-prime class vanishes on the smaller interval
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.summary: For 0<u<exp(-2/3), every changing finite class with at least two primes at or above X_N has independently vanishing normalized response for every fixed filter and ordinate.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.label: The actual three-prime class vanishes on a larger interval
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeBoun.summary: For 0<u<exp(-9/16), the entire actual class with at least three physical-cutoff primes has independently vanishing normalized response. Its exact rate is (27/8)*exp(-2533/2048)<1.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeDele.label: Both lower-degree deletions retain the whole source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszLowerDegreeDele.summary: Each deletion is applied only on its proved interval, retaining all earlier support restrictions, the exact source and the unchanged fallback elsewhere.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszIntermediatePri.label: Every nonzero survivor must contain an intermediate prime
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszIntermediatePri.summary: For 0<u<exp(-2/3), the actual support eventually forces a prime factor N^2<p<X_N. This identifies a remaining arithmetic interaction, without bounding its signed sum.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.label: The same geometric bound pays the whole large-product class
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.summary: The explicit tilt allowance applies to all labels satisfying k*L_N<=log(n), irrespective of prime count. It retains the actual coefficient, fixed filter, physical floor and uniformity in ordinate and finite selection.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.label: All actual terms at or above X_N squared vanish independently
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.summary: For 0<u<exp(-2/3), the complete actual upper class n>=X_N^2 has vanishing normalized response, with no zero premise and no restriction on its prime counts.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.label: The entire lower physical prefix has coefficient exactly zero
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.summary: For every source parameter and order, all original coefficients with n<=X_N vanish exactly. The unit, primes and nonsquarefree labels keep their original conventions.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.label: An extreme prime below X_N squared forces a prime cofactor
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalProduct.summary: A nonzero actual coefficient below X_N^2 with a prime factor at least X_N has a prime cofactor below X_N and the exact negative two-logarithm coefficient. Composite cofactors vanish by the saturated profile identity.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: The actual carrier lies in X_N<n<X_N squared
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: On u<exp(-2/3), the whole remaining support is the intersection of the previous residual and the strict physical interval X_N<n<X_N^2. Other scales retain the earlier residual.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: The physical annulus deletion loses no source-scale contribution
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: The lower deletion is exact and the upper deletion has independently vanishing normalized error. The full fixed filter and the all-scale fallback remain.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: The whole annular carrier retains negative multiplicity
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: At every exposed right-half zero, the complete actual annular carrier tends to minus the full analytic multiplicity. No source margin is lost by the physical-product pruning.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: Only the subcutoff class and intermediate/extreme semiprimes survive
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: Once N^2<X_N, a nonzero annular label either has every prime below X_N, or is p*a with N^2<a<X_N<=p and both factors prime. The latter keeps its exact signed coefficient. Their joint floor is still open.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: The annulus keeps the original coefficient and full cosine phase
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: The whole real response remains the original signed coefficient times the nonnegative factorial envelope times cos(gamma*log(n)) over actual uniquely counted integer labels.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.label: Conditional RH closure from the whole annular floor
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPhysicalAnnulus.summary: A cofinal real floor at least -c with c<1 for every whole exposed residual implies Mathlib RH. The independent joint arithmetic floor remains an explicit open premise.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszInfinitePhysica.label: The genuine infinite product tail has a geometric bound
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszInfinitePhysica.summary: Every changing infinite mask of the original coefficient with n>=X_N^2 has the same source-normalized subunit rate on 0<u<exp(-2/3), with genuine summability and every fixed filter.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.label: Separated prime ranges count each actual integer once
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.summary: A prime below X_N paired with a prime at least X_N gives at most one selected cofactor incidence at each integer label. No unordered-pair factor is silently dropped.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.label: Prime completion retains its exact physical prefix
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.summary: The completed coefficient equals the original cross-cutoff coefficient plus the physical prime prefix, retaining diagonal and repeated prefix incidences.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.label: A convergent prime head minus its genuine finite prefix
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossCompletion.summary: The cross-cutoff integer series has a proved sum equal to the completed cofactor head minus its actual prefix below X_N squared. The finite correction has no assumed cancellation.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossSupport.ev.label: The physical annulus fits all logarithmic windows
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossSupport.ev.summary: On 1/2<=u<exp(-2/3), every label X_N<n<X_N^2 eventually lies in both the original band and the narrowed log window, keeping the original damped floor.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossSupport.ev.label: Every earlier arithmetic cut is discharged for the cross class
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCrossSupport.ev.summary: Every semiprime with N^2<a<X_N<=p and p*a<X_N^2 eventually belongs to the actual annular carrier. No inherited arbitrary mask is imposed on the completed prime sum.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusCompleti.label: The actual prime-completion error is independently bounded
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusCompleti.summary: On 1/2<=u<exp(-2/3), the error between the actual annular cross class and the completed prime head minus its exact prefix is at most ((8/3)*exp(-95/96))^N times the original fixed-filter allowance. All selected intermediate primes are allowed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.an.label: The actual annulus splits without losing the shared phases
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.an.summary: The original coefficient and factorial filter give an exact sum of the all-subcutoff and uniquely counted cross-prime classes, once N^2<X_N.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.ev.label: The whole completed representation has a geometric error
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.ev.summary: The all-subcutoff response plus the completed prime head minus its physical prefix differs from the original whole annulus by the same independent geometric allowance, on 1/2<=u<exp(-2/3).

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.te.label: The joint completed response retains the full negative source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszAnnulusJoint.te.summary: At exposed right-half zeros in the proved source interval, the whole completed response tends to minus the analytic multiplicity. The independent joint floor remains open; no separate part is asserted to decay.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrefixDiagonal..label: The genuine prime-square prefix has a geometric allowance
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrefixDiagonal..summary: Every selected prime-square prefix has bound C(P,u,q)*(u/q)^N for 0<q<1, uniformly in the selected primes and height. The physical mark and single diagonal incidence are retained.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrefixDiagonal..label: All diagonal prefix terms vanish independently
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPrefixDiagonal..summary: For every 0<u<1, q=(u+1)/2 gives rate 2u/(u+1)<1 for every changing selected prime family and fixed filter. This does not extend the annular-completion source range.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefix.nor.label: The actual mixed prefix has a polynomial times geometric bound
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefix.nor.summary: For a selected intermediate prime a and a prime p<=N^2, the actual mark -log(ap)*log(a)/L_N is bounded without substituting the small-prime logarithm. Its normalized whole response is at most C(P,u,q)*(N+1)^3*tiltRate(u,q)^N.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefix.ten.label: Every mixed small/intermediate-prime prefix vanishes
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefix.ten.summary: The exact mathematically defined tilt pays the full actual mixed class on 1/2<u<exp(-1/2), for all changing selected intermediate-prime families and every fixed filter and height. No zero premise is used.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefixTran.label: Both prefix deletions preserve the complete source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszMixedPrefixTran.summary: The exact diagonal and mixed integer classes are removed with independent vanishing error. The whole refined response retains minus the full multiplicity at exposed zeros in the annular interval.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszRemainingPrefix.label: Every surviving prefix label has two distinct intermediate primes
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszRemainingPrefix.summary: The actual nonzero support after both paid deletions is a distinct-prime product with both factors in the full intermediate set. No extra completion mask is assumed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszRemainingPrefix.label: Both surviving prime incidences give the complete logarithm square
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszRemainingPrefix.summary: Unique integer labels retain both cofactor incidences. Their exact coefficient is -log(n)^2/L_N; diagonal and unordered-pair corrections are not lost.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPairedCorrectio.label: The whole carrier retains one explicit clipped prime-pair correction
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszPairedCorrectio.summary: On the annular interval, all earlier masks are discharged before the whole response becomes completed head plus unchanged unpaired subcutoff terms plus log(n)*min(1,log(n)/L_N) on distinct intermediate-prime products. Its joint signed floor is open.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralWindow.n.label: Both outer parts of the actual carrier have strict geometric bounds
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralWindow.n.summary: For 0<u<exp(-2/3), every changing divisor-majorized finite coefficient family outside 3N/2<log(n)<=8N/3 is bounded by the sum of two geometric allowances, at rates (3/2)*exp(-631/1536)<1 and (8/3)*exp(-95/96)<1. All fixed filters and phases remain.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralWindow.t.label: The actual central annulus retains the full negative source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralWindow.t.summary: Intersecting the whole actual annulus with the new central window preserves every earlier arithmetic mask and the full exposed-zero multiplicity source. Its independent central signed floor remains open.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.eve.label: The central transport pays two finite errors and keeps the whole head
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.eve.summary: On 1/2<=u<exp(-2/3), the normalized transport error is at most 2E_N with both explicit geometric rates. The completed prime head is neither truncated nor separately normed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.ten.label: The complete central representation retains the whole exposed source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.ten.summary: The three coupled components retain minus the full zero multiplicity on the annular source interval. Their independent joint lower floor remains open.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.cen.label: The actual central pair clip is one from order twenty
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.cen.summary: For u>=1/2 and N>=20, the literal floor implies L_N<=3N/2. Every central paired integer has coefficient exactly log(n), with its full phase and unique integer counting. Twenty is only this clip threshold.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.eve.label: Every nonzero unpaired survivor has at least three distinct primes
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPair.eve.summary: The actual central unpaired support retains every old arithmetic cut. The previous two-large-prime theorem and exact prime-pair classification exclude every lower prime degree eventually.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszTriplePrime.act.label: Actual three-prime coefficients have a known sign and half-logarithm bound
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszTriplePrime.act.summary: For L>0 and log(n)<=2L, every actual coefficient with exactly three distinct prime factors is nonnegative and has norm at most log(n)/2. The proof retains the third-prime difference of two full tents.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszTriplePrime.nor.label: The three-prime allowance vanishes at the reflection midpoint
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszTriplePrime.nor.summary: The same literal coefficient is bounded by (log(n)/L)*(2L-log(n)) in the upper-cutoff half of its logarithmic support. This is an independent amplitude bound, not cancellation of its oscillating sum.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.label: The actual remaining support discharges every three-prime bound premise
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.summary: The physical annulus X_N<n<X_N^2 supplies log(n)<2L_N with the integer floor kept. Every surviving three-prime coefficient therefore has the sign, half-logarithm and reflection-gap bounds without a zero premise.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.label: The whole carrier keeps four explicit prime-degree components coupled
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.summary: The exact identity retains the complete prime head, central log-weighted pair correction, actual three-prime response and actual four-or-more-prime response. No term is asserted to decay separately.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.label: The entire three-prime response pays only negative phase observations
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszCentralPrimeLay.summary: A source-normalized independent lower bound uses only max(0,-Re K), with coefficient half log(n), uniformly in height and the fixed filter. The explicit negative-phase cost is still unbounded at the source scale.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.comp.label: The exact head keeps all cofactor phases coupled
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.comp.summary: The finite complex cofactor moment remains inside each convolution order. The product logarithm shifts M=N+j+1 exactly, with every fixed filter coefficient and genuine complete prime summability.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.leng.label: The actual damped floor gives a sharper physical length
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.leng.summary: For u>=1/2 and N>=2, the original cutoff satisfies D_N+2<=2^N and L_N<=2N*log(2). This is the high-order estimate threshold, not a threshold for every prior transport.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.label: The complete high-order convolution has an independent geometric bound
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.summary: For all finite cofactor masks below log(a)<=45M/32, orders 16k>=15M have source-normalized bound (M+1)*exp(-7M/3200)*u*T*Z. The finite cofactor moment and complete prime factor retain their phases until their independent envelopes pay this component.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.label: A definite part of the actual completed head is now arithmetically bounded
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.summary: For every fixed P, uniformly in y, 1/2<=u<exp(-2/3) and N>=2, the exact high head is bounded by highHeadCost(P,u)*(N+1)^2*exp(-7N/3200). No zero, exposure or cancellation hypothesis is used.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.tend.label: The paid high head tends to zero independently
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.tend.summary: The explicit polynomial-times-geometric allowance tends to zero on the annular source interval. All original filter shifts, physical floors and complete prime orders survive.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.comp.label: Every head order is retained in an exact signed partition
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.comp.summary: The remaining 16k<15(N+j+1) orders and the independently paid high orders add to the literal completed head. Neither prime variable is truncated and the finite cofactor set is not completed.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.label: The whole signed carrier has the same independent transport allowance
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.norm.summary: The difference between the actual central joint carrier and its order-reduced representation is precisely the high head, bounded independently from N=2. Every original finite arithmetic component and support mask remains.

RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.tend.label: The remaining joint carrier retains the whole negative multiplicity source
RiemannGaussian.ZetaRieszHeadOrders.tend.summary: At an exposed zero in the annular parameter interval, the lower and middle head orders and all finite terms retain the complete negative multiplicity source. Their independent joint floor remains open.
